mechanism: Small batch on a big GPU: per-step time is dominated by kernel launches and host work, so bandwidth levers (int8) cannot help and their dequant cost shows; compile recompiles per shape bucket.
summary: Whole-process profile bundles (not benchmarks: profiler on, synthetic untemplated 64-token prompts, many requests stop early), clocks locked at 1980 MHz, MAX_BATCH_SIZE=16, 32 requests x up to 64 tokens. A, default (CUDA graphs on, no compile): 190 decode steps, median 12.55 ms, p95 17.3 ms, mean batch 6.9, 129 tok/s in the window, GPU utilization 20% mean, 135k CUDA kernels in a 2.8 s window on the 8-request run, top kernels all small elementwise/reduce ops: the decode path is launch/host bound at this batch, not bandwidth bound. B, CUSTOM_BACKEND_COMPILE=1: process wall 1210 s; 17 decode steps at ~70 s each inside the window, i.e. compilation keeps happening per step/bucket during serving, 0% utilization. C, CUSTOM_BACKEND_QUANT=int8: decode median 107.9 ms (8.6x slower than A), prefill 324 ms vs 64 ms, utilization 70%: the int8 weight-only path is compute-heavy dequant on H200, not a bandwidth win. Peak device memory 9.3-9.6 GB in all three. Numbers are facts about this config and this run; no noise band yet.
title: H200 first profiles (Gemma 4 E2B, custom-cuda): default decode 12.5 ms at ~7 rows with 20% GPU util; torch.compile cold start 20 min; int8 9x slower
triggers: before enabling CUSTOM_BACKEND_COMPILE or CUSTOM_BACKEND_QUANT=int8 on Hopper
when the eval harness measures decode on H100/H200
